In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the analysis of the moduli space of Lorentz-violative massive gravity.
the study of Lorentz-violation in gravity and its implications for the moduli space of massive gravity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the moduli space of massive gravity is a complicated manifold with several bifurcation loci.
, for a given model of massive gravity with a particular choice of the mass terms, one can nd a region in the moduli parameter space in which the theory is free of ghosts and the DVZ discontinuities.
the moduli space of Lorentz-violated massive gravity has a complicated structure with many bifurcations of different types and, in particular, the DVZ discontinuities can be avoided.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there exists a 4-dimensional subspace of mass terms in the moduli, where the ghost is absent.
the DVZ discontinuities in Lorentz-violated massive gravity are not generic.
, in the linearized approximation, one can nd a ghost-free Lorentz-violation model without any discontinuity in the Newton law, which is the same conclusion as that in Ref. [4] but in a di erent way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DVZ discontinuities are not inevitable in the massive gravity, even when the Lorentz violation is present.
the Lorentz violation can be used to discriminate the theories of massive gravity in the moduli spaces of mass terms.
the Lorentz violation can be used to avoid the DVZ discontinuities.
